resources.string: ExoPlayer plays the local test stream with Media3\'s default adaptive track selection. Pick a slower network while it plays and watch the loading rendition change first, then the one on screen once the buffer catches up.

Restart resets the network trace so every run sees the same bandwidth timeline. Startup runs from the play call to the first READY state. A stall is any BUFFERING after that which a seek did not cause. The overlay shows the rendition being downloaded and the one being decoded; they differ by the length of the buffer, so a switch is decided seconds of media ahead of what you see. Each run builds a fresh player, so no bandwidth estimate carries over. The HLS playlists declare EXT-X-INDEPENDENT-SEGMENTS: without it Media3 has to re-download the overlapping segment on every switch, and when the buffer is nearly empty it keeps the current rendition instead, so HLS stays stuck high on a slow network while DASH switches down.
